intervention: Registration drives, legal aid and payment tracking so restriction-affected workers receive statutory compensation
who_benefits: Construction workers, especially migrants and those with lapsed registration
what_it_does: Helps workers register and renew with the BOCW board, monitors payment after each GRAP closure, supports legal follow-up
evidence_reason: Loss of wages from stoppages is documented through court orders and payment records; no evaluation of registration drives on payment receipt found, but the mechanism is short and observable
india_relevance: Direct: NCR mandate exists by Supreme Court order
equity: High if it reaches unregistered migrants; low if it only serves already-registered workers
operator: Worker organisations and NGOs; welfare boards own the payment
institutional_dependencies: Welfare board data access; court orders; labour department
risks: Registration rules exclude short-term migrants; payments late; dependency on litigation
philanthropy_role: Fund outreach, monitoring and legal capacity; not the transfers themselves (statutory cess funds, 44% unspent nationally)
funder_fit: public budget; philanthropy for outreach and monitoring

intervention: Enrolment of waste pickers and sanitation workers in existing entitlements (NAMASTE profiling, municipal ID cards, Ayushman Bharat cover, OSH Code health check-ups)
category: Health and income protection (access to entitlements)
pollutant_or_pathway: Pathways A and D: illness costs and debt
who_benefits: Waste pickers and sanitation workers
what_it_does: Helps workers obtain occupational ID cards, NAMASTE profiling, PPE kits and PM-JAY health insurance, and presses municipal and contractor employers to provide statutory annual health check-ups
evidence_reason: Lung impairment among these workers is documented; schemes and duties exist but municipal ID-card issuance has lagged and coverage figures are inconsistent; no evaluation of enrolment support found, but enrolment is directly observable
equity: Reaches self-employed workers with no employer; women and Dalit workers are heavily represented in sanitation and waste work (not quantified here)
operator: Waste-picker and sanitation worker organisations; municipal corporations and NSKFDC as providers
institutional_dependencies: Municipal willingness to issue ID cards; NAMASTE implementation
risks: Cards issued without real benefits; scheme coverage stalls
philanthropy_role: Fund enrolment support, tracking of benefits received and advocacy for municipal compliance; not the insurance premiums or kits
funder_fit: public budget; philanthropy for outreach and monitoring

intervention: Design and pilot income continuity for non-construction workers affected by restrictions (vendors, delivery, small units)
who_benefits: Street vendors, platform workers, small-enterprise workers
what_it_does: Tests eligibility rules, delivery channels (e-Shram, platform social security fund, municipal vending lists) and payment triggers
evidence_reason: Testimony and surveys show income loss but no measured estimate; no Indian pilot found
india_relevance: Code on Social Security (Nov 2025) creates a fund whose benefits are not yet designed
equity: Could include women vendors and platform workers currently excluded
recurring_needs: Moderate (pilot transfers would need a public or platform payer)
operator: Labour departments; platform social security board; municipal vending committees
institutional_dependencies: New platform fund rules; GRAP triggers
risks: Philanthropy funding transfers directly would be unsustainable
philanthropy_role: Fund design, measurement of losses and a time-bound pilot with a public payer committed
funder_fit: public budget; philanthropy for outreach and monitoring

intervention: Air-pollution education embedded in school curriculum
pollutant_or_pathway: Personal behaviour: commute, windows, firecrackers, masks
who_benefits: School students and, through spillovers, peers
what_it_does: Teaches AQI, health effects and ten protective actions
evidence_reason: One two-year cluster RCT in Delhi KV schools: awareness and behaviour improved, self-reported breathing difficulty fell, effects attenuated in year two; full paper not yet available
equity: Reaches all students in a school; equity across school types untested
operator: School systems (KV Sangathan; state education departments)
risks: Effects fade without reinforcement
philanthropy_role: Fund adaptation to state schools, measurement in a second setting, and curriculum adoption support
funder_fit: public budget or employer; philanthropy for pilots

intervention: HEPA purifiers in classrooms
who_benefits: Students during school hours
what_it_does: Filters classroom air while windows and doors allow some infiltration
evidence_reason: RCT shows purifiers reduce classroom PM2.5 but health and cognitive outcomes were worse than education alone, consistent with compensating behaviour; benefit depends on room sealing, CADR, maintenance and hours of use
equity: Children in government schools lack private alternatives; electricity and filter costs fall on schools
capital_needs: Moderate (about ₹40,000 per unit cited by CEEW; ₹200-250 crore for Delhi government schools)
risks: Behavioural offset; units left off or unmaintained; does not address gases
philanthropy_role: Only as a redesigned pilot paired with behavioural messaging and maintenance budgets owned by the education department
funder_fit: public budget or employer; philanthropy for pilots

intervention: Occupational protection programmes for sanitation workers, waste pickers and roadside workers (fit-tested respirators, shift timing, health checks, employer duty)
pollutant_or_pathway: PM, black carbon at street level; waste-fire smoke
who_benefits: Sanitation workers, waste pickers, guards, delivery riders
what_it_does: Supplies and fit-tests respirators, changes shift timing away from inversion hours, adds periodic spirometry through existing schemes, and presses employers/municipalities to meet duties
evidence_reason: Exposure and lung impairment are well documented in Delhi; respirators reduce exposure when fitted and worn, but adherence in India is low and no Indian outdoor-worker trial result was found
equity: Targets the most exposed; women had lower lung function
operator: Municipal corporations and contractors (as employers); platforms; worker organisations
institutional_dependencies: Labour and municipal procurement; platform social security rules
risks: Masks without fit or replacement give false security; heat discomfort reduces use
philanthropy_role: Fund pilots with employers as co-payers and measurement of exposure and adherence
funder_fit: public budget or employer; philanthropy for pilots

intervention: Mass distribution of masks to the public
who_benefits: General public
what_it_does: One-off distribution
evidence_reason: Fitted masks reduce exposure; mass distribution in Delhi met low use and norms against wearing
equity: Untargeted
risks: Low adherence; no replacement; false reassurance
philanthropy_role: Do not fund untargeted distribution
funder_fit: public budget or employer; philanthropy for pilots

intervention: Outdoor smog towers
who_benefits: People within a few hundred metres
what_it_does: Large fans and filters in public space
evidence_reason: Independent IIT Bombay evaluation found effects mostly within 200 m; DPCC told NGT the towers were ineffective; operating cost about ₹15 lakh per month per tower
equity: Benefits whoever happens to be nearby
risks: Visible but negligible effect; diverts funds
philanthropy_role: Do not fund
funder_fit: public budget or employer; philanthropy for pilots

intervention: Anti-smog guns and water sprinklers for ambient air
who_benefits: Nearby residents
what_it_does: Sprays water mist
evidence_reason: Limited evidence of effect; covers under 0.5% of Delhi's area at planned scale; heavy water use
equity: Untargeted
recurring_needs: Electricity and 25-90 lakh litres of water a day at scale
risks: Water stress; cosmetic effect
philanthropy_role: Do not fund as an air-quality investment; support independent evaluation if government continues
funder_fit: public budget or employer; philanthropy for pilots

intervention: Filtration and cleaner-air standards in existing night shelters and childcare/health facilities
who_benefits: People experiencing homelessness; infants and patients
what_it_does: Adds sealed-room filtration to buildings that already have an operator, staff and occupants for many hours
evidence_reason: Indoor filtration lowers indoor PM where rooms are reasonably sealed; no Indian evaluation in shelters; porta-cabins and tents may leak heavily
equity: Reaches people with no private protection, but only at night and only in winter
operator: DUSIB and shelter-management agencies; health and childcare departments
institutional_dependencies: Shelter building quality; power supply; fire safety
risks: Low benefit in leaky tents; heat and ventilation trade-offs; fire risk
philanthropy_role: Fund a measured pilot in permanent shelters with the operator committing to running costs
funder_fit: public budget or employer; philanthropy for pilots

intervention: Purpose-built clean-air shelters or centres for the public
who_benefits: Intended: outdoor workers and vulnerable residents
what_it_does: Builds or designates filtered public spaces
evidence_reason: No evidence that intended users can attend without losing earnings; international evidence on shelter use and outcomes is inconclusive
equity: Outdoor workers cannot leave work to sit indoors
risks: Built but unused; no operator after grant
philanthropy_role: Investigate need before any build; prefer filtration inside services people already use
funder_fit: public budget or employer; philanthropy for pilots

intervention: Low-cost sensor networks tied to a named decision, actor and response budget
who_benefits: Residents of unmonitored districts
what_it_does: Fills monitoring gaps and triggers specific local responses (e.g. kiln inspections, burning enforcement, school advisories)
evidence_reason: Monitoring alone does not reduce exposure; AMRIT shows coverage is feasible but credibility is contested by the state board; no evidence yet of action triggered
equity: Can make rural exposure visible for the first time
risks: Data without response; disputes over accuracy
philanthropy_role: Fund only with a written response protocol and calibration against reference monitors
funder_fit: philanthropy and technical assistance

intervention: Brick-kiln conversion plus labour standards (training, piece-rate reform, housing, child-care)
category: Emission-reducing industrial upgrade plus livelihood protection
who_benefits: Kiln workers and nearby communities
what_it_does: Pairs zigzag conversion with worker training, wage records and family support
evidence_intervention: Moderate (emissions); No adequate evidence found (worker outcomes)
evidence_reason: Emission and fuel savings reported (about 75% PM/BC, 20% coal) via WRI-cited studies; worker pay, debt and exposure effects unmeasured
equity: Workers are disproportionately SC/ST migrants in debt bondage
capital_needs: Owner capital (about ₹40 lakh per kiln, 1-2 year payback)
operator: Kiln owners (capital); labour and pollution boards (standards); NGOs (worker support)
risks: Cleaner kilns with unchanged bondage; owners pass costs to workers
philanthropy_role: Fund worker-side components and independent measurement; owners finance conversion
funder_fit: public, concessional or private finance; philanthropy for transition support

intervention: Sustained clean cooking use (refill support, women's decision-making, last-mile supply)
pollutant_or_pathway: Household PM2.5 and CO; residential share of ambient
who_benefits: Women, infants and children in biomass-using households
what_it_does: Moves PMUY households from occasional to exclusive LPG or electric cooking
evidence_reason: HAPIN cut personal PM2.5 by about two-thirds but found no birthweight, stunting or clear lung-function effect, likely because exposure stayed high; household fuel is a large ambient source in Patna and rural Bihar
equity: Refill cost and autonomy barriers fall on poor women
recurring_needs: High (fuel subsidy is a public responsibility)
operator: Oil marketing companies; state governments; World Bank UP programme
risks: Health benefits may not appear unless ambient pollution also falls
philanthropy_role: Support delivery research and women's access within government programmes; do not fund fuel
funder_fit: public, concessional or private finance; philanthropy for transition support

intervention: Crop-residue management machinery subsidies
who_benefits: Rural residents of Punjab/Haryana; downwind populations
what_it_does: Subsidises balers, happy seeders and similar
evidence_reason: Fire counts fell sharply alongside machinery, enforcement and straw markets; attribution between these is not established
equity: Subsidy reaches farm owners; labourers and smallholders' costs unmeasured
risks: Satellite undercounting; enforcement burden on smallholders
philanthropy_role: No philanthropic gap in capital; possible role in independent distributional evaluation
funder_fit: public, concessional or private finance; philanthropy for transition support

intervention: Primary-care readiness and sentinel surveillance for pollution episodes
who_benefits: Patients in high-exposure districts
what_it_does: Clinical protocols, surveillance and advice to vulnerable patients during episodes
evidence_reason: National programme exists (per snippets) but coverage and effect not documented; Indian time-series shows mortality rises on high-pollution days
equity: Public facilities serve those without private care
risks: Surveillance without response
philanthropy_role: Fund a district demonstration with the health department owning recurrent costs
funder_fit: public health budget; philanthropy for demonstration

intervention: Independent evaluation and spending accountability for government clean-air measures
who_benefits: Public; decision-makers
what_it_does: Commissions evaluations like the IIT Bombay smog-tower study before scale-up; tracks NCAP fund use and outcomes
evidence_reason: Repeated pattern of visible measures scaled without evidence (towers, guns) and under-used funds; evaluations have changed decisions (DPCC on towers)
equity: Indirect benefit to all; can include distributional analysis
operator: Universities and think tanks with public data access
risks: Evaluations ignored; perceived as hostile
philanthropy_role: Fund an independent evaluation facility with pre-agreed government use
funder_fit: philanthropy and technical assistance

intervention: Worker and community organising on air quality (AQI ambassadors, registration support, local advocacy)
approach: Enable exposure reduction and access to entitlements
who_benefits: Women construction workers; informal settlement residents
what_it_does: Builds knowledge and collective voice to claim protections
evidence_reason: Outputs documented (75+ women trained, registrations, government health camps reported); no independent outcome evaluation
equity: Centres women and marginalised groups
risks: Dependence on grants; burnout
philanthropy_role: Fund as part of portfolios with outcome measurement
funder_fit: philanthropy and technical assistance

intervention: Replacing old diesel buses with electric or cleaner fleets, run under franchise contracts
pollutant_or_pathway: Vehicle exhaust (PM2.5, black carbon, NO2) on bus corridors
who_benefits: Bus users, roadside workers and residents along routes
what_it_does: Swaps polluting diesel buses for electric ones with depots and charging, operated under service contracts
evidence_reason: Vehicles are a large measured source in Jakarta, Delhi and Lahore; the programmes found (Dhaka 400 buses, Punjab 600 buses) are approved but not yet evaluated for street-level air quality
india_relevance: Direct (Uttar Pradesh, Haryana programmes); regional (Bangladesh, Pakistan, Philippines)
equity: Benefits depend on routes serving low-income areas and on fares
operator: City transport authorities and franchised operators
institutional_dependencies: Franchise contracts; electricity supply; fare policy
risks: Climate benefits assumed to equal air benefits; buses added without retiring old ones
philanthropy_role: Fund independent measurement of roadside exposure before and after, and fare and route equity analysis; not the buses
funder_fit: public, concessional finance

intervention: Vehicle inspection and emissions testing centres
who_benefits: Roadside workers and residents
what_it_does: Tests vehicles and removes or repairs high emitters
evidence_reason: Dhaka's project funds five new and two upgraded centres plus 20 mobile units; outcomes not yet published
equity: Costs can fall on owners of old commercial vehicles, often low-income drivers
risks: Paper compliance; burden on low-income drivers without support
philanthropy_role: Fund monitoring of testing integrity and support schemes for low-income drivers
funder_fit: public budget, concessional finance

intervention: Continuous emissions monitoring of large industrial sources, linked to enforcement and public disclosure
who_benefits: Residents near industrial belts
what_it_does: Streams real-time emissions data to regulators so limits can be enforced and data disclosed
evidence_reason: India mandates online monitoring for 17 industry categories; Bangladesh's project will operationalise a programme; no evaluation of effect on emissions found
equity: Helps industrial-belt communities if data are public and acted on
operator: Pollution control boards; Department of Environment (Bangladesh)
risks: Data without enforcement; tampering
philanthropy_role: Fund independent analysis of disclosed data and community access
funder_fit: public budget; philanthropy for data use

intervention: Finance and technical help for small and medium firms to switch boilers and furnaces to electric, modern biomass or controlled systems
pollutant_or_pathway: Industrial and commercial combustion (brick, cement and others)
who_benefits: Residents near industry; workers in the firms
what_it_does: Combines clean-technology finance, incentives and technical assistance for about 400 enterprises (Nepal)
evidence_reason: Nepal's 2026 project is approved; no results yet; kiln conversion evidence (Bihar) suggests large emission cuts are possible but worker effects are unmeasured
india_relevance: Regional (Nepal); relevant to Indian SME clusters
equity: Firms may pass costs to workers or close
risks: Low uptake; worker displacement
philanthropy_role: Fund worker-side safeguards and independent measurement
funder_fit: concessional finance plus grants

intervention: Paying for or collecting crop residue so farmers do not burn it
who_benefits: Rural residents; downwind cities
what_it_does: Creates buyers, machinery services or payments for residue (Thailand purchase agreements; Punjab super seeders; Cambodia straw management)
evidence_reason: Fire counts fell sharply in Indian Punjab alongside machinery and enforcement, but causes are not separated; Thailand reports self-measured pilot volumes; no independent evaluation found
equity: Smallholders and labourers may be left out of machinery and contracts
risks: Markets collapse when subsidies end; penalties fall on smallholders
philanthropy_role: Fund distributional evaluation and smallholder access
funder_fit: public budget, private purchase, blended

intervention: Airshed-wide clean-air plans that coordinate states, provinces and countries
pollutant_or_pathway: Regional pollution travelling hundreds of kilometres
who_benefits: Everyone in the airshed
what_it_does: Coordinates measures across sectors and upwind regions rather than city by city
evidence_reason: Modelling shows South Asian PM2.5 comes from upwind sources hundreds of kilometres away and that coordinated action is most cost-effective; Uttar Pradesh has India's first airshed-based plan; delivered results not yet evaluated
equity: Depends on which sectors carry costs
operator: State and national governments; regional platforms
risks: Plans without budgets
philanthropy_role: Fund technical support and independent tracking of plan delivery
funder_fit: public budget; technical assistance; philanthropy

intervention: Community-led air monitoring that feeds into local decisions
pollutant_or_pathway: Local hotspots invisible to official monitors
who_benefits: Residents near waste sites, informal settlements, outdoor workers
what_it_does: Trains residents to measure air (fixed or wearable monitors) and use the data with authorities
evidence_reason: Funded projects in the Philippines and Indonesia documented exceedances missed by official networks; effects on policy are reported by the funder, not independently evaluated
india_relevance: Regional (Philippines, Indonesia); relevant to Delhi settlements
equity: Centres groups excluded from official data
risks: Data dismissed as non-regulatory
philanthropy_role: Fund monitoring tied to a named decision and calibration
funder_fit: philanthropy
